ABOUT THE ROLE 

The Automation Software Engineer is a technical problem solver who works directly with business teams to understand operational problems and opportunities and turn them into practical technical solutions. The engineer participates throughout the full lifecycle, including discovery, requirements, workflow analysis, solution design, prototyping, development, integration, testing, rollout, adoption, stabilization, and continuous improvement, combining software engineering with business analysis, solution design, systems thinking, integration engineering, and implementation.



Business users often understand the problem or desired outcome before detailed requirements or a technical solution exist, and the engineer is expected to help define both. This is a highly collaborative, business-facing engineering role, not a heads-down development position, and it requires comfort working with technical and nontechnical colleagues across Operations, Clinical, Finance, HR, Data, IT, and other functions. The role still demands strong software engineering capabilities and discipline, with alignment to enterprise architecture, security, privacy, and compliance standards.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

Business Discovery and Solution Design

 - Work directly with business users and stakeholders to understand current workflows, pain points, desired outcomes, roles, business rules, decision points, exceptions, data requirements, system dependencies, and success criteria.

 - Lead discovery and solutioning when requirements are incomplete or evolving by asking effective questions, uncovering unstated requirements, and challenging assumptions, then translate business problems into requirements, user stories, process designs, prototypes, and technical designs rather than waiting for completed specifications.

 - Design improved future-state workflows and technical solutions, simplifying or redesigning processes before automating them and determining the right combination of process change, existing platforms, automation, integration, and custom software.



Software and Automation Engineering

 - Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain internal applications, APIs, integration services, automations, and reusable software components.

 - Apply sound engineering principles including modular design, maintainability, code quality, error handling, logging, documentation, observability, scalability, and supportability.

 - Choose the appropriate approach for each business problem, whether configuring an existing platform, using an automation tool, developing an integration, building an internal application, or writing custom software, favoring reusable capabilities over one-off solutions.



Solution Delivery and Adoption

 - Work iteratively with business stakeholders throughout implementation, demonstrating prototypes and working solutions, validating requirements and design decisions, and incorporating feedback during development rather than at the end.

 - Coordinate user acceptance testing and partner with business owners and end users on rollout planning, documentation, communications, training, and readiness appropriate to the solution.

 - Stay engaged after launch to monitor adoption and effectiveness, gather feedback, resolve issues, stabilize the solution, confirm intended business outcomes were achieved, and identify opportunities for continued improvement.



Integration and Platform Development

 - Build and maintain integrations using REST APIs, webhooks, JSON, authentication protocols, service accounts, connectors, scheduled exchanges, and event-driven patterns across enterprise platforms.

 - Develop reliable data mappings, transformations, validation, exception handling, retries, monitoring, and reconciliation to keep integrations dependable.

 - Work with technologies such as Microsoft Graph, Entra ID, Azure services, enterprise SaaS platforms, data platforms, and healthcare systems, partnering with platform owners, data engineers, infrastructure, security, and vendors as appropriate.



Software Development Lifecycle and Production Reliability

 - Participate in backlog refinement, estimation, technical design reviews, and peer code review, using Git-based source control, branching, and pull requests.

 - Develop appropriate unit, integration, regression, and end-to-end tests, and use CI/CD, environment management, release management, and disciplined production deployment practices.

 - Support production solutions through monitoring, alerting, debugging, troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis, while maintaining architecture documentation, API documentation, data mappings, runbooks, release notes, testing documentation, and support procedures.



AI-Assisted Engineering

 - Use AI-assisted engineering tools throughout the engineering workflow to accelerate business and technical analysis, prototyping, development, integration work, testing, debugging, troubleshooting, refactoring, and documentation.

 - Provide AI-assisted engineering tools with sufficient business, workflow, architectural, and technical context, and critically review, test, debug, and improve AI-generated code rather than accepting output without validation.

 - Apply the same standards to AI-assisted development as to other development, including source control, peer review, testing, architecture, deployment, security, documentation, and accountability; AI accelerates the engineer but does not replace engineering judgment, and the engineer helps establish reusable AI-assisted engineering patterns and standards.



Team Collaboration and Continuous Improvement

 - Collaborate closely with AI & Automation team members and partners across technology and the business throughout discovery, solution design, development, implementation, and improvement.

 - Participate actively in solutioning sessions, technical design reviews, architecture discussions, planning activities, retrospectives, and peer reviews, sharing reusable patterns, lessons learned, and engineering guidance.

 - Measure and improve solution outcomes such as reduced manual effort, simplified workflows, improved cycle time, adoption, reliability, data quality, user experience, and avoided cost.

 

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR 

 - Bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, information systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.

 - Three to five years of professional software-development experience, including delivering and supporting production software as part of a development team.

 - Proficiency in at least one modern programming language such as Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, C#, or Java, and working knowledge of SQL and data structures.

 - Experience with software design, source control, Git, branching, pull requests, peer review, testing, debugging, CI/CD, deployment, and production support.

 - Hands-on experience developing integrations using REST APIs, webhooks, JSON, authentication methods, data mapping, validation, monitoring, and error handling.

 - Experience translating business processes and operational problems into technical requirements and working solutions.

 - Experience working directly with nontechnical users and business stakeholders through discovery, prototyping, testing, implementation, and post-launch improvement, and communicating technical concepts clearly to them.

 - Demonstrated experience discovering and clarifying requirements, rather than only implementing predefined specifications, and operating effectively when problems are incomplete, evolving, or ambiguous.

 - Strong analytical, troubleshooting, communication, and technical-documentation skills.

 - Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, in a professional or substantive software-development workflow, including supplying technical and business context, reviewing generated code, testing and debugging outputs, refactoring solutions, using Git and pull-request workflows, and applying peer review and engineering standards.



Preferred Requirements

 - Experience with Workato, Microsoft, MuleSoft, Boomi, or similar integration and automation platforms.

 - Experience building internal business applications, workflow platforms, integration services, or operational tools.

 - Experience with Microsoft Azure services such as Azure Functions, App Service, API Management, Service Bus, Logic Apps, Key Vault, Application Insights, or related services.

 - Experience with Microsoft Graph, Entra ID, Microsoft 365, Teams, SharePoint, or Power Platform integrations.

 - Experience with containerization, cloud application hosting, automated testing frameworks, observability tools, infrastructure-as-code, or secure software-development practices.

 - Experience integrating enterprise platforms such as Asana, Salesforce, NetSuite, ADP, HRIS systems, ITSM tools, EHR-related platforms, contact-center systems, or data warehouses.

 - Experience with agentic engineering tools, MCP integrations, AI agents, or LLM-enabled applications.

 - Experience working in healthcare, behavioral health, or another regulated industry.
